2_Introduction: With the improved uniformity of SAM, the SAM-based devices showed a maximum PCE of 25.6476%, with a VOC of 1.1799 V, FF of 81.4827%, and JSC of 26.678 mA/cm². The perovskite precursor solutions were prepared using 1.65 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0. Specifically, the perovskite precursor solution was first spun at 1000 rpm for 5 s, and then at 5500 rpm for 30 s. During the second step, 150 µL of chlorobenzene was dropped on the spinning substrate 15 s before the end of the process. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cells arise from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and interfacial electronic engineering: the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₅FA₀.₉PbI₃.₀ formulation optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and octahedral distortion to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and halide segregation, with the low A-site cation disorder (90% FA⁺) enhancing lattice cohesion and reducing dynamic ion migration pathways; this compositional foundation is translated into high-quality films through precisely tuned spin-coating dynamics—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) spreading ensures uniform precursor wetting and minimizes coffee-ring effects, while the high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) phase governs solvent evaporation rate and supersaturation buildup, with chlorobenzene antisolvent quenching applied at the critical 15-s mark to trigger instantaneous nucleation across the entire substrate, thereby enabling homogeneous domain formation and suppressing stochastic grain boundary defects; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives complete solvent removal, promotes Ostwald ripening for grain enlargement, and facilitates iodide redistribution to heal undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites at grain surfaces and interfaces—processes whose efficacy is directly corroborated by image-derived characterization showing near-unity film coverage (>99.2%), minimal pinhole density (<0.04 µm⁻²), and spatially uniform grayscale intensity in PL mapping, which collectively indicate suppressed non-radiative recombination centers and continuous charge percolation pathways; concurrently, the improved SAM uniformity—evidenced by reduced interfacial roughness and enhanced dipole alignment in XPS and UPS—modulates the work function of the underlying charge transport layer, passivates interfacial dangling bonds via strong anchoring (e.g., phosphonic acid or silane groups), and introduces a favorable interfacial dipole that aligns energy levels to minimize extraction barriers and suppress interfacial recombination; the synergy between the stoichiometrically robust perovskite lattice, kinetically optimized crystallization, and uniformly distributed SAM monolayer thus jointly suppresses bulk trap states (as reflected in prolonged average PL lifetime τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 µs and monoexponential decay kinetics), eliminates interfacial energetic mismatches, and mitigates residual strain (confirmed by absence of PbI₂ (001) peak at 12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) perovskite reflection in XRD), culminating in VOC of 1.1799 V, JSC of 26.678 mA/cm², FF of 81.4827%, and PCE of 25.6476%.
